full_judgment:
Obaidul Hassan J. This Criminal Petition for leave to Appeal has arisen out of the judgment and order dated 17.06.2021 passed by the High Court Division in Criminal Miscellaneous Case No.1064 of 2021 making the Rule absolute. 

 2. The accused respondent filed Criminal Miscellaneous Case No.1064 of 2021 before the High Court Division stating, inter alia, that on 29.06.2018 one Md. Mokbul Hossain, Sub-Inspector, Netrakona Police Station, Netrakona as informant lodged a First Information Report (hereinafter referred to as the FIR) with the Officer-in-Charge of Netrakona Police Station. The informant lodged the FIR alleging, inter alia, that while on 29.06.2018 the informant along with his force was in special operation for recovery of illegal drugs, execution of warrant at 03:05 hours at Teribazar Mor under Netrakona Pourashava, he received a secret information that a person was selling drugs on the road in front of the cosmetic and grocery shop of one Sohel Miah located at Purbo Medni Bazar under Netrakona Police Station. After getting this information, the informant informed the matter to his higher authority and reached at the above mentioned place at 03:40 hours and arrested the accused person. Police recovered 73 grams of heroin wrapped with white colour polythene from the body of the accused, which is worth about Tk.7,30,000.00. Thereafter, on 29.06.2018 at about 03.55 hours the informant prepared a seizure list and took the signature of the witnesses on it. 

 4. After submission of the charge sheet, the case was transferred to the Court of Sessions Judge, Netrakona and the same was numbered as Sessions Case No. 672 of 2018 and the learned Sessions Judge took cognizance of the offence against the accused under Table 1 (ICha) of section 19 (1) the Narcotics Control Act, 1990. Thereafter the case record was transmitted to the Court of Additional Sessions Judge, Netrakona for trial and disposal. 

 7. Being aggrieved by and dissatisfied with the order of rejection of prayer for bail in Sessions Case No. 672 of 2018, arising out of G.R Case No. 409 (2) of 2018, corresponding to Netrokona Police Station Case No. 117 dated 29.06.2018, under Table 1(Kha) of Section 19 (1) of the Narcotics Control Act, 1990 now pending before the Court of learned Additional Sessions Judge, Netrokona; the accused respondent filed Criminal Miscellaneous Case No.1064 of 2021 before the High Court Division of the Bangladesh Supreme Court, and the High Court Division was pleased to issue Rule. After hearing, the High Court Division made the Rule absolute by its judgment and order dated 17.06.2021. 

 9. Mr. Biswajit Debnath, the learned Deputy Attorney General, appearing on behalf of the petitioner, has taken us through the judgment and order passed by the High Court Division, the relevant provisions of the Narcotics Control Act, 1990, the connected materials on record and submits that the judgment and order passed by the High Court Division making the Rule absolute clearly shows it's non-application of judicial mind. The High Court Division failed to appreciate that the accused-respondent is named in the FIR having strong prima-facie and specific overt act of committing heinous offence under Table 1(Kha) of Section 19 (1) of the Narcotics Control Act, 1990 from whose exclusive control and possession 73 grams of heroin was recovered. He further submits that the case is under trial and at this stage the interim order of bail will totally frustrate the purpose of prosecution case creating obstacle in the way of free/fair trial. 

 11. We have heard the learned advocates appearing on behalf of both the parties, the relevant provisions of law and the connected materials on record. From the materials on record, it appears that the name of the accused respondent has been mentioned in the FIR and it has also been mentioned that on search, 73 grams of heroin was recovered from the left fist of his wearing lungi wrapped with white coloured polythene and it suggests that the said amount of heroin was recovered from his exclusive possession. In the instant case, the chemical examination report of the seized heroin has been collected. In the report, it has been opined that in the seized brown coloured powder presence of heroin has been detected. 

 12. During investigation a prima fade case against the accused respondent has emerged. To destroy the youth generation narcotics is a dangerous tool. Keeping or selling narcotic is crimes against the society as a whole. From the Charge sheet submitted by the investigating officer, it appears to us that various cases are pending against the accused in Netrakona Sadar Thana. In this circumstance, if the accused respondent is enlarged on bail, then he would be harmful for the society and he may create obstruction in trial.
